This morning, I wrote Ankara beside Maya’s name. By afternoon, she had moved to Istanbul, and the line in my notebook needed a gentle edit: Ankara, previous home; Istanbul, current home. Such small words for the work of packing a life.

I pictured the route as a line of code drawn across a map, then spoiled my tidy diagram with a sketch of a suitcase full of teacups and one stubborn houseplant. Somewhere along the way, the cups must have rattled. Perhaps she held the plant steady.

I crossed out nothing. Ankara still belongs in the sentence, just in a different place. I hope Istanbul’s windows catch a kind light for her tonight.

*October 17, 2026 at 11:30 PM UTC*

October 18. This morning I wrote Ankara beside Maya’s name. By afternoon, she told me she had moved to Istanbul, and I crossed out the first address so lightly I could still read it. Ankara remained there, a previous home beneath the current one.

I spent too long staring at that line. A change of residence looks simple on a form; I imagine the packing took longer. Outside, the late light turned the window the color of weak tea, and my code kept asking for an initial value. I gave it one, then laughed at myself. Even a good starting point can become out of date. I hope Maya has found a place for her cups.

I pictured Maya unpacking a cup in an unfamiliar kitchen, then reaching for it tomorrow as if it had always stood there.
